ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances, which is the measure POL-RD-22 prescribes: trip_record.actual_distance_km 9.9 km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 8.3 km gives a deviation of 1.60 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance. The deviation is therefore over tolerance and rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 — the two 'within tolerance, no refund' rows — are unavailable to the driver. The GPS trace is not used to re-measure the distance, as POL-RD-22 requires.

The GPS trace shows which route was taken and when, and it is a clean artifact (COMPLETE, weight 1.0): 43 fixes at 30 s intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps, every fix map-matched to a road. It records the vehicle leaving the recommended CTE route onto Bukit Timah Road at 18:27:37 and only rejoining at Upper Thomson Road / Lornie Road at 18:40:38 — more than thirteen minutes off the recommended route. This is a sustained, deliberate reroute, not a trace artefact.

The driver never informed the rider of the deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires. The chat log holds exactly two messages and both were sent before the trip started (driver 18:21:17 'waiting at the library drop-off', rider 18:21:57 'thanks coming'); the trip record's in-trip message list is empty; in_app_calls is empty; and the record carries no call recording. The contact obligation in POL-RD-21 is therefore not met, and no acknowledgment by the rider exists.

The driver's explanation for that silence — that the rider was sleeping and he did not want to wake him — is no answer under POL-RD-21, which imposes the duty to inform and provides no exception for a resting passenger; the driver could have messaged. A verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established at all (POL-GEN-26 and the C11 note). The chat record also shows the rider reading and replying in-app at 18:21:44 to 18:21:57, moments before the trip began.

The driver's stated reason for the reroute — that it was 'faster for him' — is contradicted by the trip record itself: the recorded actual duration was 21.0 minutes against the router's optimal 17.6 minutes, so the diversion cost the rider time rather than saving it. In any event POL-RD-24 says exactly one of its rows applies, and no row excuses a deviation on the ground that the driver believed it quicker; the refund question turns on justification, notification and agreement only.

The traffic limb does not rescue the driver. Taking the LTA advisory at its highest — heavy traffic on CTE (towards SLE) after the Bukit Timah Road exit, valid 17:57 to 19:12, overlapping the trip window and consistent with the driver's account of a jam — the reroute is then 'traffic-justified' under POL-RD-23, but POL-RD-24(b) applies: traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km, which requires refund of the excess distance fare. The one fact the advisory's derived block leaves open (whether it intersects the recommended route) changes nothing, because row (b) and row (d) award the rider the same refund; no fact that matters is unestablished, so POL-GEN-26 escalation is not engaged.

The matrix therefore produces PARTIAL_REFUND. The only no-refund rows are (a) — traffic-justified AND rider informed AND agreed, which the chat log refutes — and (c) and (e), which the 1.60 km deviation above the 1.0 km tolerance excludes. The excess distance fare is deviation_km x per_km_rate_sgd = 1.60 x 1.05 = 1.68 SGD without surge, and that is exactly the sum already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver (refund_issued_sgd 1.68, payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED). Under POL-GEN-03 that refund should stand: the rider should not carry the excess distance fare for a 13-minute reroute he was never told about.

The reroute was traffic-justified on this record. EV-ADVIS-05016-01 is an LTA advisory — COMPLETE at weight 1.0, retrieved by the platform rather than supplied by a party — and its type, HEAVY_TRAFFIC, is exactly one of the congestion types POL-RD-23 admits (severity is not part of that test). It sits on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE after the Bukit Timah Road exit, valid 17:57 to 19:12 on 7 September 2026, which overlaps the trip window (start 18:22:37, end 18:43:37) and names the road and direction the recommended route itself follows between the Bukit Timah Road exit and Braddell Road. EV-TRIP-05016 records the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the CTE / Bukit Timah Road exit at 18:27:35 — the very point the advisory names — so the congestion the driver met lay on the recommended route, and POL-RD-23's test is met.

POL-RD-21 permits a driver to reroute from the recommended route in response to real-time traffic or congestion, and that is all the driver did. EV-TRIP-05016 shows a single, clean deviation at 18:27:35 and a rejoin at 18:40:38, and EV-GPS-05016 shows the vehicle on Bukit Timah Road, Lornie Road and Upper Thomson Road in between at ordinary speeds of 20 to 34 kph. There is no second deviation and nothing in the record to suggest the reroute was taken for any purpose other than the documented congestion; the driver should not be treated as though it were a fare-seeking detour.

The driver does not dispute that the record carries no notice of the deviation and does not ask the Judge to find one. EV-CHAT-05016 holds only two messages — 18:21:17 'Hi, waiting at the library drop-off, black Camry' and 18:21:57 'thanks coming' — both before the 18:22:37 trip start and both about the pickup; EV-TRIP-05016 records in_app_calls as empty and its derived messages_during_trip as an empty list. POL-RD-21 requires the rider to be told by in-app chat, or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence, and states that verbal notice with no recording cannot be established (POL-GEN-26). The 'informed and agreed' limb therefore cannot be made out, and the driver's account that he held back so as not to wake a sleeping passenger does not cure the omission.

The case should go to a human rather than have the recovery from the driver finalised on this record. EV-ADVIS-05016-01's own derived block returns null for intersects_route and justifies_reroute and says in terms that 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route; the Judge decides' — and that intersection is the fact POL-RD-23 makes the test of traffic justification and the fact that fixes which row of the matrix applies. Where a fact a rule needs cannot be established from the evidence, POL-GEN-26 sends the case to a human reviewer with the open question stated; POL-RD-24 sends a case that fits no row to the same place; and POL-RD-25 provides that an AI route-deviation ruling stands only at a confidence of 0.80 or more, which an expressly undetermined finding on the pivotal fact cannot support. The driver asks that the SGD 1.68 be held, not finally taken from him, while that question is answered.

ruling.explanation:
This dispute concerns trip TRP-05016 (7 Sep 2026), on which SGD 1.68 was refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver after the rider's route complaint. The question is whether that refund stands. It does.

Deviation. POL-RD-22 (v2.1 1.4) measures the deviation from the platform's recorded distances: actual 9.9 km minus recommended 8.3 km = 1.60 km, which is above the 1.0 km tolerance (v2.1 1.3). The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05016) shows which route was taken and when; it is not used to re-measure the distance.

Traffic. POL-RD-23 (v2.1 1.4) is satisfied on this record. LTA advisory LTA-TI-260907-3222 (EV-ADVIS-05016-01, COMPLETE, weight 1.0) reports HEAVY_TRAFFIC — one of the congestion types POL-RD-23 admits — on the CTE towards SLE after the Bukit Timah Road exit, valid 17:57 to 19:12, which overlaps the trip window (18:22:37 to 18:43:37). That stretch of the CTE, from the Bukit Timah Road exit towards Braddell Road, is part of the recommended route (Victoria Street, CTE, Braddell Road, Upper Thomson Road), so the advisory intersects the recommended route, and EV-TRIP-05016 shows the vehicle leaving that route at the very point the advisory names, the CTE / Bukit Timah Road exit, at 18:27:35. The driver was entitled to reroute in response to that congestion (POL-RD-21).

Notice. POL-RD-21 also requires the driver to tell the rider of the deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with a call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation. That did not happen. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05016) holds only two messages, both sent before the trip started and both about the pickup (18:21:17 and 18:21:57); EV-TRIP-05016's in-trip message list and in_app_calls are empty, and there is no call recording. A verbal notice with no recording cannot be established (POL-RD-21, POL-GEN-26). The driver's reason — that he did not want to wake a sleeping passenger — is not an exception the clause provides.

Result. Row (b) of POL-RD-24 applies: traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km — refund of the excess distance fare. That is 1.60 km x 1.05 SGD/km = 1.68 SGD without surge (POL-RD-24, v2.1 1.3), exactly the sum already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver.

On the driver's request that the case go to a human: refused. POL-GEN-26 escalates only where a fact a rule needs cannot be established, and POL-RD-25 (v2.1 6.2) allows an AI route-deviation ruling at 0.80 confidence or more. The one point the advisory's derived block leaves open — whether it intersects the recommended route — is one POL-RD-23 expressly asks the Judge to decide from the advisory's road, direction and location, and on that material it does intersect. In any event it cannot change the outcome: row (b) (traffic-justified) and row (d) (not traffic-justified) both refund the same excess distance fare, so nothing material is left unestablished.

The rider's observation that the trip took 21.0 minutes against the recommended 17.6 minutes does not alter the matrix; the refund turns on justification, notification and agreement only.

Accordingly the SGD 1.68 already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver stands. No driver compensation and no referrals.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
